reason: The hypothesis relies on a chain of mechanistic claims (size mismatch → lattice distortion → phonon modification → Tc change), but the cited evidence only addresses the final link (disorder and superconductivity in a different HEA system) and a calculation of size mismatch in an unrelated alloy; it does not provide direct support for the specific premises about tuning distortion or its effect on phonons and electron–phonon coupling in the proposed Ti–Zr–Hf–Mo–V system.
premises: Atomic size mismatch in HEAs can be systematically tuned by substituting elements with different atomic radii.
Increased atomic size mismatch enhances lattice distortion and local strain fields.
Lattice distortion modifies the phonon spectrum.
Changes in the phonon spectrum alter electron–phonon coupling and thus Tc in BCS superconductors.
The cited evidence supports a connection between disorder and superconductivity in related HEA systems.
